All society does is make it more or less acceptable for people to be open about it. We haven't been keeping track of gayness for very long, but the data we have supports this.

According to the General Social Survey, "the percentage of Americans reporting predominately same-sex partners remained stable between 1991 and 2010. In contrast, the percentage who reported ever having a same-sex partner increased, especially among women." In other words, there aren't any more people leading a predominantly gay lifestyle than there used to be, there's just more people acting on their sexual curiosity.

I'd also like to point your attention to a study recently published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. In the study, psychologists conducted an experiment designed to cross-reference participants' aggression towards homosexuals with their upbringing, self-reported sexuality, and latent sexual desires. Turns out, people who self-identify as straight but show signs of gay desires are also the most likely to show hostility toward gays, especially if they had an authoritarian upbringing.

The rest of us aren't especially threatened by two guys playing with each others' dongs in the privacy of their homes.
